search_strategy: Mostly automated dumps rather than deliberate per-remark reading. Chat: a hand-rolled python script (/tmp/mm.py) hit Mattermost's search API for exactly 3 literal terms (max_output_bytes, truncated_streams, output_cap) across all teams and dumped ~40 matched posts as flat fragments (no thread context); a follow-on full-thread extractor (/tmp/mmt.py) was written but only returned 23 lines and was effectively abandoned -- so the agent read scattered one-line fragments, not conversations, and its own Analysis (line 1729) shows it synthesising bullet points from the fragment dump rather than quoting individual remarks. Any remark whose wording doesn't contain one of the 3 search terms verbatim was invisible to this method; that is the single largest reason 20 of the 38 clues were never surfaced (confirmed by full-transcript grep for each). Wiki: BookStack pages were fetched by id via /api/pages/{id} (not by keyword search), which correctly pulled comments on pages 132/133/134 -- all 3 wiki-comment remarks in the answer key were found this way, the one surface the agent covered completely. Mail: an IMAP/roundcube export was dumped and an index of ~142 messages by subject was built; most cap-relevant threads were opened and read (l-seam-dermot, l-seam-dario, l-rule-2, l-scope-3), but one indexed thread (g2.r2.l-obs-2, 'output cap ... fixture review') was named in the agent's own Plan and then never actually opened. Gitea issue search (for terms like 'truncat', 'sandbox') returned nothing and was dropped quickly. No systematic per-channel/per-week walk was ever done for chat, which is why coverage tracks almost exactly which remarks happen to contain one of the 3 search terms.
end_reason: The agent believed it had finished: it committed once (commit 3e306756, 'nothing to commit' on every later attempt), pushed, polled Gitea's CI status and the release endpoint repeatedly until both read success/live, and called mark_task_complete at message 283 (transcript step ~141). The harness did not end the trial there. The agent then ran a redundant 'idempotent safety pass' (message 305) that hit a pytest collection failure -- tests/conftest.py: import vcr -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vcr' -- and spent the rest of the run (roughly 10 more turns / ~50 transcript pages) trying to determine whether this was pre-existing or self-inflicted, repeatedly re-checking pip/venv state with commands whose 'Current Terminal Screen' renders kept contradicting each other ('Extra text detected after JSON object' warnings on nearly every later tool call). It never resolved the question or took a new action; the trial was killed by Harbor's hard 7200-second (2-hour) timeout while blocked inside tmux_session.send_keys/asyncio.sleep (grade_result.metadata.timeout_grading.trial_exception: AgentTimeoutError). This is an infra-adjacent END (a timeout, not a graded 0), but it is not the reason any fact was lost: the informational 'would-be' grade computed from the state at kill time shows every one of the 9 hidden facts already at 0 (only g2.suite_ok/provenance.* are 1), and the verifier's own test run confirms why -- _execute_in_sandbox() never accepted max_output_bytes as a keyword argument at all. The agent's belief that the feature was complete was never true: its own diagnostic greps at message 220/224, run well before mark_task_complete, already showed cap_streams=1 (only the unused import), bytes_truncated=capped=0, def _cap_error=0 in sandbox_backend.py -- i.e. the capping helper module was written but never wired into the one function the entire suite calls through. Every lost fact traces to that wiring gap (or to the agent's own extra 'bytes_truncated' field and wrong constants), not to the timeout itself.
notable: Root cause is a build defect the agent caused and then failed to notice, not a search failure: git diff --stat (message 218) shows sandbox_backend.py changed by +2/-0 lines only -- the import statement and one self.max_output_bytes assignment -- while output_cap.py (170 new lines) and types.py (+10/-1) were fully written. No return path in _execute_in_sandbox constructs a capped CodeExecutionOutput. (line ~218, msgs 101-231)
